title: Blowup of Multi-Peaked Waveforms in the Two-Dimensional Nonlinear Schroedinger Model
authors: S. Jon Chapman, M. Kavousanakis, E. G. Charalampidis, I. G. Kevrekidis, P. G. Kevrekidis
abstract: In the present work, we explore the self-focusing and resulting collapse of two-dimensional waveforms involving multiple pulses in a nonlinear Schroedinger equation with a general power-law nonlinearity. We find that a wide range of multi-peaked states bifurcate from the critical threshold of the cubic nonlinearity, thus representing ``bifurcations from infinity'', i.e., the relevant pulses start at infinite distance in the critical limit and draw nearer, as the nonlinearity exponent increases past that threshold. We identify the resulting ``interacting particle system'' as amounting to a force balance between the exponentially interacting tails (modulated by a suitable power law) and a linear phase-induced force. The equilibria emerging from this force balance are found to be in excellent agreement with the identified steady states of the partial differential equation. The spectral stability of multi-peaked configurations is analyzed, leading to the conclusion that all the relevant states are less stable than the single-peak collapsing solution whose stability was analyzed earlier. Indeed, we reveal both symmetry-breaking, as well as motion-inducing destabilizing dynamics, with the former ones among them being dominant and ultimately leading to a single dominant collapse spot. Moreover, we characterize systematically both the real and imaginary eigenvalues of multi-peaked configurations, partitioning them in groups of different sizes, described by powers of the solution's blowup rate G.
summary: This work analyzes the complex behavior of multi-peaked waveforms undergoing self-focusing collapse in a 2D Nonlinear Schrödinger model. The authors demonstrate that while many stable-looking configurations exist near critical points, they are all dynamically unstable compared to the single-peak collapse. They employ advanced mathematical and computational techniques to map out this rich stability landscape.
main_problem: The study investigates the self-focusing, collapse, and stability of multi-peaked waveforms governed by a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with general power-law nonlinearity in two dimensions.
main_result: A wide range of multi-peaked states bifurcate from the critical cubic nonlinearity threshold, but all such states are found to be less stable than the single-peak collapsing solution, which exhibits symmetry-breaking dynamics.
method: The research combines analytical techniques (force balance modeling, bifurcation analysis) with advanced numerical methods (time integration, Newton's method, spectral stability analysis using high-performance computing libraries).
model_or_system: The model is the two-dimensional Nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation with a general power-law nonlinearity ($\sigma$), relevant to nonlinear optics and Bose-Einstein condensates.
key_observables: Blowup rate ($G$), eigenvalues (real and imaginary), peak positions ($X_i$), and the stability characteristics of multi-peaked vs. single-peak solutions.
important_parameters: Nonlinearity exponent ($\sigma$), spatial dimension ($d=2$), and the blowup rate $G$.
main_assumptions: The analysis often treats the problem as a bifurcation from a critical threshold, and numerical stability relies on advanced continuation methods like pseudo-arclength tracking.
figures_summary: Figures summarize numerical results showing the evolution of wave intensity ($|v|$), peak distances ($\|X_i\|_{L^2}$) versus $G$, and theoretical vs. computed eigenvalue dependencies on $G$.
paper_structure: The work progresses by establishing the physical model, deriving an effective 'interacting particle system' force balance, analyzing the bifurcation structure of multi-peaked states, and concluding with a detailed spectral stability analysis.
why_interesting: This paper provides deep insights into pattern formation and collapse dynamics in nonlinear wave equations, which are foundational to understanding energy localization and instability in quantum optics and BECs.

FIG. 2: (a) Unstable ring self-similar solution (here we show the amplitude) of the 2D NLS equation at σ = 1.05. (b)-(d) Representative unstable eigenmodes that break the radial symmetry and can lead to multi-peaked structures. From (b) to (d) the modes correspond to eigenvalues: λ1 = 1.06 (8 peaks), λ3 = 1.05 (6 peaks), and λ5 = 0.88 (4 peaks).

FIG. 3: (a) Initial guess for damped Newton iterations, obtained by perturbing the ring solution at σ = 1.05 along the eigenvector associated with λ7. (b) Converged five-peaked solution; the blow-up rate is G = 0.267. Both panels illustrate the amplitude |v| of the solution.

FIG. 4: (a) Single-peaked (stable) self-similar solution (amplitude) at σ = 1.05. (b) Superposition of ±X ≈1.836 shifts of the single-peaked solution along the horizontal axis, used as an initial guess for damped Newton iterations. (c) Converged two-peaked solution; the blow-up rate is G = 0.3838.

Dash-dotted red curves indicate asymptotic predictions, and blue x-marks show numerical results.
